goal: Push the T-shaped block (without lifting it) until it lies exactly on top of the gray T-shaped pad, with the same position and orientation, then return the arms to their start pose.
instruction_templates: Push the T-shaped block to align it precisely with the gray T-shaped pad.
success: Orientation: the angular distance between the full 3D orientations of block t and pad target_t is < 7 deg.
Position: the XY distance between the root position of t and the root position of target_t is < 0.007 m (7 mm, strict).

Both target arms are back at origin: all target arms (left_arm and right_arm; the support arm is not counted) have their end-effector pose within 0.15 m on EACH axis (|dx|,|dy|,|dz| all <= 0.15 m) and within 20 degrees (quaternion angle) of the pose they had at the start of the episode (recorded after the scene settled).
The above three hold simultaneously after one action.

Lift constraint (query, must stay 0 for the whole episode): the block t must never be higher than 0.01 m above its initial z (root z at the start of the episode, measured every action); a single action at which z(t) - z0 > 0.01 m fails the episode immediately.
evaluation: Single stage, checked after every action; the three alignment/arm conditions must hold at the same time. The reward manager is evaluated only once per action (after the sim sub-steps of that action are finished), never between sub-steps. In each evaluation the FIRST pending stage of the check list is tested (every condition in it, all at that same moment; a condition that is a nested list is an OR); when it passes it is removed permanently (never re-verified later) and the next stage becomes pending; at most one stage is removed per action. Reward is 1.0 only when the check list is empty (and no query/trigger counter is violated); the episode is declared a success as soon as reward >= 0.999 after an action, and ends as a failure if the action counter reaches step_lim without that, or earlier if the environment is flagged failed (query counter exceeded, see below). No final_check list is registered by this task, so the final-check logic at step_lim adds nothing. The lift query is evaluated after every action; as soon as the counter exceeds the aim of 0 the environment is flagged failed and the episode ends as a failure.
objects: t: the T-shaped block (Rigid, 1; 't' category model 1), table-frame x in [-0.45,0.45], y in [-0.25,-0.1], random yaw over the full 360 deg
target_t: the gray T-shaped pad ('t_cushion', Geometry, static, 1), same x/y ranges as the block, random yaw over the full 360 deg

clutter: 20 distractor objects (two clutter groups of 10, category-unique): group A x in [-0.6,0.6], y in [-0.5,-0.25] or [0.0,0.5]; group B x in [-0.6,-0.45] or [0.45,0.6], y in [-0.25,0.0]; random yaw up to +-30 deg, margin 0.015; a prohibited rectangle x [-0.35,0.35], y [-0.5,-0.4] (near the robot) is kept free
end_requirements: Both arms within 0.15 m per axis and 20 deg of their start pose at the same action as the block alignment (position < 7 mm, orientation < 7 deg).
notes: Very strict tolerance: 7 mm and 7 deg. The orientation test is the full-quaternion angle (so a tilted block would also fail), and the block's root point (not an edge) is compared with the pad's root. The block may not be lifted more than 1 cm at any time, so grasping and carrying it is effectively prohibited (small tilts or hops above 1 cm during pushing also fail). The pad is a static geometry on the table and is not an obstacle (the block can be pushed over it). The random variant uses a different T model (index 1) and adds clutter distractors that can obstruct pushing paths.
